ranking.tie_break: Equal scores: pattern fit (business school or faculty, small public team), then quality of evidence.

who.t: 5y: analyst-to-associate, junior auditor/senior associate, risk or fintech product roles. 10y: vice president, senior manager (audit), portfolio manager, fintech team lead. 20y: director or managing director, partner (audit), CFO/CRO-line roles. UNVERIFIED as a cohort fact.
Hubs: Amsterdam (Zuidas), Utrecht, Rotterdam, Frankfurt, London, Luxembourg, Zurich, Brussels; Limburg and Aachen/Cologne area UNVERIFIED (no source).
Most UM alumni work in a field-matching sector.

wants.t: Vetted deal-flow of talent (interns, juniors) at low screening cost
Peer network across firms and cities
Status visible internally (e.g. "mentor of the year")

refuses.t: Open DM inbox, sales pitches from fintech peers, broadcasting views on markets

inbox.t: Reply to cold C-level outreach is about 7%.
Yes-triggers: fixed 20-30 minute slot, pre-filled agenda, specific question, evidence of preparation. Time-box figures are a practitioner norm, UNVERIFIED as measured preferences.

incentives.t: Employer CSR-hour rules by firm not retrieved (UNVERIFIED)

objections.t: All Dutch bank staff must take the banker's oath or affirmation; unlawful disclosure of inside information is prohibited (MAR art. 14).
No market-sensitive talk in group chat; chat banner "no client or deal information"; declared-conflict field (employer, competitor). Time is the largest barrier.

mechanics.t: Contact rules (strongest fit), status points as access ticket, small events (one slot), map by hub city. Open group chat: weak fit because of MAR risk.

alumni_types.name: Management
alumni_types.sub: general management, operations, entrepreneurs, corporate leadership

who.t: 5y: management trainee, operations/product manager, junior founder. 10y: head of function, business unit manager, founder/co-founder. 20y: managing director, COO/CEO of SME, board member, serial entrepreneur. UNVERIFIED.
Cities: Randstad, Brabant (Eindhoven region), Limburg, Duesseldorf/Cologne, Brussels, London, Berlin, Singapore for internationals.

wants.t: Access to talent; peers outside their own company; founder-to-founder introductions; recognition

refuses.t: Administrative requests, event fatigue, "pick my brain" asks

inbox.t: About 7% reply to cold C-level outreach.
Entrepreneurs are fastest to reply when the ask is a hiring or customer opportunity; a student-only ask needs a very small box (15-20 min) and a stated outcome.

incentives.t: Hiring juniors and interns; reputation inside the university network

objections.t: Time; fear of being asked for a job or investment; business confidentiality (low compared with B1/B3)
44% of interested US alumni would mentor, so willingness exists; format preference not reported by profession.

mechanics.t: Map, events by city, mentor flag with capacity limit, project-based tutoring/challenge with a company case, status points converting to "featured company" visibility.

alumni_types.name: Law
alumni_types.sub: corporate and tax lawyers, in-house counsel, legal advisers

who.t: 5y: associate / junior in-house. 10y: senior associate, counsel, senior in-house counsel. 20y: partner, general counsel, judge/regulator roles. UNVERIFIED.
Cities: Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague, Brussels, Luxembourg, London, Frankfurt. UM has a law faculty; which faculty supplies this segment for UniCircle is UNVERIFIED.

wants.t: Peers for referrals across jurisdictions; clean, prepared junior candidates; visibility

refuses.t: Any channel that could touch client information; unsolicited requests for legal advice (also a professional-liability issue)

inbox.t: High protection: confidentiality is a core value for lawyers.
Yes-trigger: CV-first, scoped question ("how did you choose tax vs corporate"), 20-minute slot.

incentives.t: Dutch firms publish pro bono volumes (one firm: 8,500+ hours, 75 matters, 211 lawyers in 2023); no mandatory pro bono hours and no CPD credit; some firms count pro bono toward billable targets (older survey).
Student mentoring could be framed as a firm social-impact activity if the firm accepts it; UNVERIFIED that firms count mentoring.

objections.t: Five core values incl. independence, integrity, confidentiality (Advocatenwet art. 10a).
Conflict of interest is a live issue (a lawyer should not mentor a student who works for an opposing party): add a conflict-declaration field and a "no legal advice" disclaimer.

mechanics.t: Contact rules and mentor opt-in with topic whitelist; events with an explicit no-client-talk rule; group chat only as moderated topic rooms; points as quiet status, not leaderboards.

alumni_types.name: Consultancy
alumni_types.sub: strategy and management consulting, Big Four advisory

who.t: Career blogs describe analyst-to-partner timelines of about 7-12 years at top strategy firms with high attrition before partner (a former consultant estimates about 90% leave before partner).
5y: consultant / senior consultant; 10y: manager / senior manager or industry exit; 20y: partner or C-suite in industry. Cities: Amsterdam, Utrecht, Duesseldorf, Frankfurt, London, Zurich, Brussels.

wants.t: Recruitment pipeline, alumni-of-firm networks, client introductions after exit

refuses.t: Case-interview requests in bulk; free consulting for students' companies

inbox.t: Consultants are used to structured asks: short written brief, 30 minutes, specific deliverable (e.g. review a case answer).

incentives.t: Recruiting credit (referrals), personal brand, giving back; Big Four CSR hours UNVERIFIED (search returned nothing).

objections.t: Time (billable utilisation), client confidentiality and independence rules for audit-linked advisory, conflict when a client is the student's employer.

mechanics.t: Case clinics / mock-case mentoring slots (tutoring format), event nights by city, points that unlock "approach" with a message template, contact rules with weekly cap.

student_types.name: Red: action-oriented
student_types.evidence_strength: low-med (gamification S4/S5 real, type link UNVERIFIED)

observable.t: First click: "find a mentor / internship / who works at X" or a direct message button; short outcome-first asks; skips profile completion; short sessions; high repeat if a result arrives within a day. Hypotheses to test.

wants.t: Fast results, outcome intros; tutoring quick answers (risk of "executive help-seeking": gets the answer, learns less); mentoring: one concrete ask answered within 48h; project groups with a deadline; pitch nights, case competitions
Executive help-seeking relates negatively to achievement.

mechanics.t: Task-style progress toward "right to approach"; team (collaborative) leaderboards, not individual. Onboarding: "What do you want to do in the next 4 weeks?" with 3 outcome buttons; short tone.

Gamification effects are small, stable for cognitive outcomes; competition plus collaboration worked best for behaviour. One course: leaderboard plus badges lowered intrinsic motivation, satisfaction and exam scores.

objections.t: Ranking can crowd out autonomy; risk of gaming points via low-quality tutoring (quantity over quality).

observable.t: First click: read how points and contact rules work, check mentor profile depth, filters; precise questions; long sessions with low message volume; drafts messages and abandons; reads FAQ before first request. Hypotheses to test.

wants.t: Depth, accuracy, clear rules; tutoring explanations with sources and time to reflect; a mentor with matching field and a written agenda; small structured peer groups; seated events with a topic and Q&A

mechanics.t: Message templates, "preview what the mentor sees", private progress not rank; show how contact rules protect alumni; precise tone with the reason for each field; no countdown timers.
Narrative gamification beat points/badges/leaderboards in motivation (a 2026 meta-analysis seen only as a search summary, UNVERIFIED); SDT predicts controlling rewards weaken autonomy.

objections.t: Public ranking most likely raises anxiety; perfectionism blocks first contact, so the first ask must be small.

observable.t: First click: tutorial-group or city group, people tab, chat; asks "who else is going / who from my group"; high message volume; low conversion to formal requests unless introduced; shares the event with friends. Hypotheses to test.

wants.t: Belonging, groups; group tutoring and peer-buddy; group mentoring and alumni "office hours" with 5-8 students; tutorial-group channels; referrals via friends; social repeat events
Students prefer informal help from friends over formal sources.

mechanics.t: Tutorial-group channels, group mentoring, team/group points and thank-you signals; onboarding "Which tutorial group / city / society are you in?"; warm tone; invite-a-friend; group streaks.
Relatedness is a basic need; competition combined with collaboration was effective for behavioural outcomes.

objections.t: Public ranking excludes low-ranked members and promotes cliques, especially in mixed-nationality groups.

student_caveat: Colour types are a working heuristic, not a psychometric claim. Independent evidence for DISC-style types is weak (S1), the similar MBTI falls short of test standards (S2), and learning-style matching has no adequate evidence base (S3). A colour label must not be treated as a fact about a person, gate access, be shown to others, or be used for selection or grading. Legitimate uses: design hypotheses tested with behaviour data, behaviour-based "modes", self-selected preferences that can change, all options offered to all users.
